meta.title: Pair Pocket: mine, yours and ours, in two currencies
meta.description: A household ledger for couples who share some money and keep some apart. Personal and shared ledgers, CAD and KRW side by side, free, with no bank connection.
meta.ogAlt: Pair Pocket: mine, yours and ours, in two currencies

hero.h1: Mine, yours and ours, in two currencies.
hero.sub: A household ledger for couples who share some money and keep some apart. Canadian dollars and Korean won, side by side.

story.h2: Most money apps assume one country and one person.
story.p1: I moved to Canada and still hold money in more than one country. Every app I tried was built for a single market, or treated the two of us as one person.
story.p2: I wanted mine, yours and ours in one place, in two currencies, without my private entries showing up on my partner's screen. I could not find that, so I built it.
story.p3: Bank statements make it harder. They show money moving under a code nobody remembers six months later. Pair Pocket lets you record the story behind the money instead.

ledgers.h: Your book, their book, and the one you share.
ledgers.p1: Each person keeps a private personal ledger. Partners link a shared ledger on top. Switch between them with one tap, and look at Canada, Korea or both with exchange rates.
ledgers.p2: What you keep personal stays personal. If you ever unlink, the shared history never reaches a new partner.

add.p: Merchants and categories you used before are suggested as you type. Bring in a lot at once with a CSV file, and export one whenever you want.

scan.p: A photo or a statement screenshot becomes a draft entry, and you check it before it is saved. AI is optional and runs on your own free Gemini key. Manual entry and CSV import work without one.

settle.p: Paid for a shared expense from your own account? Settle it with money from a personal account, or the other way around. Both sides are written together, so the books always agree.

moves.p: Card payments, transfers between your accounts and money going between the personal and shared ledgers stay in the history but are not counted as spending. Your charts show what you actually spent, not the same money twice.

subs.p: Subscriptions, bills and installments, with promo pricing, skipped payments and reminder emails. Move one between personal and shared when life changes.

stocks.p: Track brokerage accounts with live quotes and currency conversion, right next to the rest of your money.

invite.p: Pick a shared ledger start date so both of you line up from day one. Once they accept, the shared ledger is ready.

try.p: You paid for a shared grocery run with your own card. Slide to settle it from the shared account and watch where the money goes.
try.note: Charts count the expense once, however it is settled.
try.fallback: Example: a CA$86.00 grocery bill paid on your card. Settle CA$86.00 from the shared account. Your personal account gets CA$86.00 back, the shared account drops by CA$86.00, nothing is left to settle, and your charts still count CA$86.00 once.

free.h2: Free, private, and clear about it.

rows.text: bank connections, on purpose. Bank aggregation is a paid service, and a free app cannot honestly offer it.
passwords stored. You sign in with Google.
currencies side by side, Canadian dollars and Korean won.
languages in full, English and Korean, and it installs on your phone like an app.

built.h2: Built end to end by one person.
built.p: Pair Pocket is a production app, not a mockup. I designed it, built it and run it.
built.stack: Next.js on Vercel, FastAPI on Heroku, MongoDB Atlas, Google Gemini.

items.d: Every read is scoped to the person or the partnership and fails closed, so a partner's private history never reaches shared suggestions.
Transfers and settlements write both sides in one database transaction. If the second write fails, the first rolls back.
Short-lived access tokens with a rotating, revocable refresh cookie.
Model output goes through a review screen, and each person's key is encrypted at rest.
Every pull request runs lint, a translation check, a production build and the backend tests.

cta.p: Sign in with Google. Link your partner whenever you are ready.
cta.dialogDesc: Dual-currency (KRW/CAD) shared and personal ledgers. Sign in with your Google account.

footer.starH: Like what you see? Star it on GitHub.
footer.starP: The code is on GitHub, and a star helps other couples find it.
